canonicalName: Higher-form and non-invertible symmetries in quantum field theory

milestones.label: Higher-form symmetries defined
milestones.work: D. Gaiotto et al., Generalized Global Symmetries, arXiv:1412.5148 (2014)
milestones.description: The paper defines q-form global symmetries using extended charged operators.

evidence.claim: First public version posted in December 2014

milestones.label: Non-invertible topological operators extend the framework
milestones.work: B. Heidenreich et al., Non-Invertible Global Symmetries and Completeness of the Spectrum, arXiv:2104.07036 (2021)
milestones.description: Non-invertible operators are used to connect charge completeness and absence of global symmetries.

evidence.claim: First public version posted in April 2021; abstract states the extension

milestones.label: Non-invertible symmetries applied to QED and QCD
milestones.work: Y. Choi, H. T. Lam and S.-H. Shao, Non-invertible Global Symmetries in the Standard Model, arXiv:2205.05086 (2022)
milestones.description: The paper applies non-invertible operators to QED and QCD selection rules and reframes the neutral-pion decay coupling.

evidence.claim: First public version posted in May 2022; abstract specifies QED, QCD and pion coupling

notes: The event spans distinct higher-form and non-invertible phases. The 2022 paper is a documented physical application, not a proven first application of all generalized symmetries. No named field institution was verified.

canonicalName: Fractal uncertainty principle and quantum chaos

milestones.label: Fractal uncertainty principle named in spectral-gap work
milestones.work: S. Dyatlov and J. Zahl, Spectral gaps, additive energy, and a fractal uncertainty principle, arXiv:1504.06589 (2015)
milestones.description: The public paper introduces a fractal uncertainty principle in its spectral-gap argument.

evidence.claim: First public version posted in April 2015

milestones.note: The same paper states and applies the principle.

milestones.label: Fractal uncertainty used for hyperbolic spectral gaps
milestones.work: S. Dyatlov and J. Zahl, Spectral gaps, additive energy, and a fractal uncertainty principle, arXiv:1504.06589 (2015)
milestones.description: The method yields an essential spectral gap for convex co-compact hyperbolic manifolds under the paper's dimension conditions.

evidence.claim: Abstract explicitly identifies the spectral-gap application

milestones.note: The same paper truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

milestones.label: Spectral gaps without the pressure condition
milestones.work: J. Bourgain and S. Dyatlov, Spectral gaps without the pressure condition, arXiv:1612.09040 (2016)
milestones.description: A stronger fractal uncertainty result gives gaps for all convex co-compact hyperbolic surfaces.

evidence.claim: First public version posted in December 2016; abstract names fractal uncertainty as the new ingredient

milestones.label: Survey of fractal uncertainty and quantum chaos
milestones.work: S. Dyatlov, An introduction to fractal uncertainty principle, arXiv:1903.02599 (2019)
milestones.description: The survey systematically presents the principle and its quantum-chaos applications.

evidence.claim: Public survey preprint posted in March 2019

works.citation: Spectral gaps, additive energy, and a fractal uncertainty principle

notes: The 2015 Dyatlov–Zahl paper is earlier than the inherited 2016 Bourgain–Dyatlov citation. The later paper proves a broader surface result.

milestones.label: Croot–Lev–Pach polynomial method
milestones.work: E. Croot, V. Lev and P. Pach, Progression-free sets in Z_4^n are exponentially small, arXiv:1605.01506 (2016)
milestones.description: The precursor applies a polynomial argument to progression-free sets in a different group.

milestones.label: Exponential cap-set bound posted
milestones.work: J. S. Ellenberg and D. Gijswijt, On large subsets of F_q^n with no three-term arithmetic progression, arXiv:1605.09223 (2016)
milestones.description: The note states an exponential bound, including the F3 cap-set problem.
milestones.note: The same note states and applies the transferred method.

milestones.label: Polynomial method applied to cap sets
milestones.work: J. S. Ellenberg and D. Gijswijt, On large subsets of F_q^n with no three-term arithmetic progression, arXiv:1605.09223 (2016)
milestones.description: The authors explicitly use the Croot–Lev–Pach method to bound cap sets.

evidence.claim: The abstract names the method and target problem

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

works.citation: On large subsets of F_q^n with no three-term arithmetic progression
works.whyItMatters: Co-applies the polynomial method to cap sets

notes: The Croot–Lev–Pach paper is a method precursor for a different ambient group; the cap-set result is the later Ellenberg–Gijswijt note. No independent field institution is asserted.

milestones.label: Integral p-adic Hodge theory announced
milestones.work: B. Bhatt, M. Morrow and P. Scholze, Integral p-adic Hodge theory—announcement, arXiv:1507.08129 (2015)
milestones.description: The announcement sketches an interpolating cohomology theory before prisms were defined.

milestones.label: Prisms and prismatic site introduced
milestones.work: B. Bhatt and P. Scholze, Prisms and Prismatic Cohomology, arXiv:1905.08229 (2019)
milestones.description: The preprint defines prisms and attaches the prismatic site to p-adic formal schemes.
milestones.note: The same paper defines the theory and proves applications.

milestones.label: Prismatic cohomology proves comparison results
milestones.work: B. Bhatt and P. Scholze, Prisms and Prismatic Cohomology, arXiv:1905.08229 (2019)
milestones.description: The paper applies the theory to almost purity, q-de Rham cohomology and p-adic Tate-twist vanishing.
milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

notes: The 2015 announcement and 2016 full integral-Hodge paper are precursors, not the first use of 'prismatic'. The Annals 2022 issue publishes the already public 2019 work; it is not counted as a separate conceptual milestone.

canonicalName: Undecidability in quantum games via combinatorial group theory

milestones.label: Solution-group embedding and game undecidability
milestones.work: W. Slofstra, Tsirelson's problem and an embedding theorem for groups arising from non-local games, arXiv:1606.03140 (2016)
milestones.description: The paper embeds finitely presented groups into solution groups and states undecidability for perfect commuting-operator strategies.
milestones.note: The same paper develops and applies the embedding theorem.

milestones.label: Group embedding applied to nonlocal games
milestones.work: W. Slofstra, Tsirelson's problem and an embedding theorem for groups arising from non-local games, arXiv:1606.03140 (2016)
milestones.description: The solution-group construction gives nonlocal games separating commuting and tensor-product strategies.
milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

milestones.label: Quantum correlation set shown non-closed
milestones.work: W. Slofstra, The set of quantum correlations is not closed, arXiv:1703.08618 (2017)
milestones.description: A linear-system game separates a limit of finite-dimensional strategies from any finite-dimensional perfect strategy.

milestones.label: MIP*=RE gives stronger undecidability
milestones.work: Z. Ji et al., MIP*=RE, arXiv:2001.04383 (2020)
milestones.description: The result reduces the halting problem to deciding the entangled value of a nonlocal game.

works.citation: Tsirelson's problem and an embedding theorem for groups arising from non-local games
works.whyItMatters: Transfers solution-group embedding to nonlocal games

notes: The inherited arXiv:1709.05032 points to a different paper by Dykema, Paulsen and Prakash. Slofstra's non-closure paper is arXiv:1703.08618. The 2017 paper's later version adds finite-dimensional undecidability; do not backdate that particular statement to version 1 without checking it.

milestones.label: Neural tangent kernel defined
milestones.work: A. Jacot, F. Gabriel and C. Hongler, Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks, arXiv:1806.07572 (2018)
milestones.description: The preprint defines the NTK for neural-network training.
milestones.note: The same paper defines and uses the kernel.

milestones.label: NTK used to analyze training and generalization
milestones.work: A. Jacot, F. Gabriel and C. Hongler, Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks, arXiv:1806.07572 (2018)
milestones.description: The authors describe infinite-width gradient descent through kernel dynamics and analyze convergence.

evidence.claim: The abstract explicitly describes training dynamics

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

milestones.label: NTK spectra analyzed
milestones.work: G. Yang and H. Salman, A Fine-Grained Spectral Perspective on Neural Networks, arXiv:1907.10599 (2019)
milestones.description: Spectral analysis of the NTK studies learning bias and generalization across architectures.

works.citation: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
works.whyItMatters: Co-introduces the NTK and its training analysis

notes: This record covers the neural tangent kernel, not the entire mean-field theory of neural networks. The inherited summary conflates related but distinct infinite-width regimes.

milestones.label: Matroid Hodge theory proves log-concavity
milestones.work: K. Adiprasito, J. Huh and E. Katz, Hodge Theory for Combinatorial Geometries, arXiv:1511.02888 (2015)
milestones.description: The earlier matroid Hodge theorem motivates later Lorentzian-polynomial methods.

milestones.label: Lorentzian polynomial class developed
milestones.work: P. Brändén and J. Huh, Lorentzian polynomials, arXiv:1902.03719 (2019)
milestones.description: The preprint defines the class and connects it to matroids and M-convex sets.
milestones.note: The same paper defines the class and proves major applications.

milestones.label: Lorentzian method proves strongest Mason conjecture
milestones.work: P. Brändén and J. Huh, Lorentzian polynomials, arXiv:1902.03719 (2019)
milestones.description: The paper applies Lorentzian-polynomial theory to the homogenized matroid Tutte polynomial and strongest Mason conjecture.

evidence.claim: The abstract explicitly states these applications

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

notes: The checked founding preprint was posted in 2019. The catalogue's 2018 start was not promoted without a matching public record; the 2020 Annals issue is a later publication of the same work.

milestones.label: Ax–Schanuel for Hodge variations
milestones.work: B. Bakker and J. Tsimerman, The Ax-Schanuel conjecture for variations of Hodge structures, arXiv:1712.05088 (2017)
milestones.description: A related period-map transcendence theorem predates the tame-topology paper.

milestones.label: Arithmetic quotients shown o-minimally definable
milestones.work: B. Bakker, B. Klingler and J. Tsimerman, Tame topology of arithmetic quotients and algebraicity of Hodge loci, arXiv:1810.04801 (2018)
milestones.description: The paper develops the tame-topology framework for arithmetic quotients and period maps.
milestones.note: The same paper states the framework and applies it.

milestones.label: Definability applied to Hodge loci
milestones.work: B. Bakker, B. Klingler and J. Tsimerman, Tame topology of arithmetic quotients and algebraicity of Hodge loci, arXiv:1810.04801 (2018)
milestones.description: The authors derive algebraicity statements for Hodge loci using o-minimal definability.

evidence.claim: The abstract names the Hodge-locus application

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

works.citation: Tame topology of arithmetic quotients and algebraicity of Hodge loci
works.whyItMatters: Co-develops and applies o-minimal Hodge methods

notes: The event summary mixes the 2017 Ax–Schanuel theorem with the 2018 tame-topology work. The former is retained as a related precursor, not asserted to be an o-minimal application.

canonicalName: Synthetic Lorentzian curvature from optimal transport (non-smooth singularity theorems)

milestones.label: Transport entropy characterizes smooth strong energy condition
milestones.work: R. J. McCann, Displacement convexity of Boltzmann's entropy characterizes the strong energy condition from general relativity, arXiv:1808.01536 (2018)
milestones.description: A smooth-spacetime transport characterization precedes the synthetic extension.

milestones.label: Synthetic timelike Ricci bounds formulated
milestones.work: F. Cavalletti and A. Mondino, Optimal transport in Lorentzian synthetic spaces, synthetic timelike Ricci curvature lower bounds and applications, arXiv:2004.08934 (2020)
milestones.description: The preprint defines timelike Ricci lower bounds using transport in Lorentzian synthetic spaces.
milestones.note: The same paper formulates and applies synthetic curvature bounds.

milestones.label: Synthetic curvature applied to Lorentzian comparison
milestones.work: F. Cavalletti and A. Mondino, Optimal transport in Lorentzian synthetic spaces, synthetic timelike Ricci curvature lower bounds and applications, arXiv:2004.08934 (2020)
milestones.description: The paper uses the new transport bounds for geometric comparison applications in Lorentzian length spaces.

evidence.claim: The paper's title and abstract identify applications

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

milestones.label: Synthetic null hypersurfaces studied
milestones.work: F. Cavalletti, A. Mondino and E. Manini, On the geometry of synthetic null hypersurfaces, arXiv:2506.04934 (2025)
milestones.description: The later paper develops geometry of null hypersurfaces in the synthetic setting.

works.citation: Optimal transport in Lorentzian synthetic spaces, synthetic timelike Ricci curvature lower bounds and applications
works.whyItMatters: Co-formulates and applies synthetic timelike Ricci bounds

notes: The catalogue's claim that the cited 2025 null-hypersurface paper reproves Hawking–Penrose singularity theorems is unsupported by that citation and is not repeated here. A separate source is needed for the singularity-theorem part of the event name.

milestones.label: Condensed abelian groups publicly described
milestones.description: A public institute seminar abstract describes condensed abelian groups and solid completion as joint work.

evidence.claim: The MPIM seminar record dated September 2019 contains the public abstract

milestones.note: This seminar abstract is a public statement, but the first publication date of the original course notes remains to be independently pinned down.

milestones.label: Named Bonn course on condensed mathematics
milestones.description: Bonn lists a summer-term course and notes with the field name.

evidence.claim: Scholze's official lecture-notes index identifies the course as SS 19

milestones.note: The currently hosted PDF is a 2026 update and is not used to date the original document.

milestones.label: Condensed vector spaces used for functional-analysis theorem
milestones.description: The liquid-vector-space theorem is presented as a key application of condensed mathematics to functional analysis.

evidence.claim: Scholze's public note sets out the liquid-vector-space theorem and its application

milestones.note: This records a documented application, not a proven first application of every condensed construction. The 2020 note has no checked bibliographic record, so the work field remains empty.

works.citation: Lectures on Condensed Mathematics (updated citable edition)
works.whyItMatters: Presents the joint Clausen–Scholze framework; this work entry refers specifically to the 2026 edition

notes: The 2019 course and public seminar are independently documented, but the currently citable arXiv edition of the lecture notes is from 2026. The original 2019 notes' publication date remains uncertain. The 2020 public liquid-tensor note is an application rather than a firstness proof.
